description: Committee recommended new van rates reflecting higher operating costs.
Committee recommended payment terminal 'come into force' date.
Committee recommended options to improve driver safety by September 2026.

chips.text: Recommended
Councillor Donauer cautioned against over-regulating private enterprise for driver safety.
Taxi drivers and franchise owners expressed concerns about payment delays and earnings.
Administration noted payment schedules are not prescribed in bylaw, left to companies.
Administration could not provide specific numbers on van trips needed to recoup costs.
Taxi drivers highlighted safety concerns, mentioning a driver killed in March.
Van rates considered for customers with disabilities, seniors, or medical issues.

speakers.name: Malik Draz
speakers.organization: Taxi Drivers and Franchise Owners Association of Saskatoon
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Amendments to Vehicles for Hire Bylaw
said: Opposes amendment 5 on point-of-sale machines; causes delayed driver payments.
New van rate regulations will unfairly decrease taxi driver earnings.
Taxi fares are regulated, unlike ride-share; supports cameras for safety.

speakers.name: Adnan Ahmad
speakers.summary: Registered to speak on: Amendments to The Vehicles for Hire Bylaw
said: Van rates should apply based on customer needs, not just passenger count.
Airport flat rates for vans are unclear; offer meter or flat rate choice.
Emphasizes driver safety; supports cash in advance payment to reduce violence.
